title: The New Student's First Day
summary: A boy who just moved to a new city feels nervous on his first day at a new school, until a classmate's small act of kindness helps him start to feel at home.
poll: A small act of kindness, like sharing a seat at lunch, can make a big difference to someone new.

versions.title: The New Student's First Day
versions.text:
Yusuf moves to a new city. Today is his first day. It is a new school. He feels nervous. He does not know anyone.

Yusuf walks into his room. The kids have friends. He has none. He sits in the back. He feels alone.

It is lunch time. Yusuf has a problem. He does not know where to sit. Every table is full. He stands there. He feels worried.

A classmate named Omar sees him. Omar is kind. He waves. He makes room. "Come sit with us," he says. Yusuf feels happy. He sits down.

After lunch, Omar helps him. He shows the books. He shows the yard. He shows the rooms.

Yusuf feels less nervous now. He has a kind new friend. The school feels like home.

It is lunchtime. Yusuf does not know where to sit. Every table looks full. He stands there with his tray. He feels worried.

A classmate named Omar sees Yusuf standing alone. Omar is a kind boy. He waves. He makes room at his table. "Come sit with us," he says with a smile. Yusuf feels relieved. He sits down.

After lunch, Omar helps Yusuf. He shows the books. He shows the yard. He shows the rooms.

Yusuf feels much less nervous now. He has made a kind new friend. The school already feels more like home.

versions.title: The New Student's First Day
versions.text:
On his first day at a brand-new school, Yusuf feels very nervous. His family just moved to this busy city. He does not know a single person here.

Yusuf walks slowly into his classroom, trying not to look nervous. The other students already have friends and groups to sit with. He sits quietly in the back row, feeling alone.

At lunchtime, Yusuf has no idea where to sit. Every table in the busy cafeteria looks full. Students are talking and laughing together. He stands there holding his tray, feeling worried.

A classmate named Omar notices Yusuf standing alone with nowhere to go. Omar is a kind, friendly boy. He waves and quickly makes room at his crowded table. "Come sit with us," he says with a warm smile. A wave of relief washes over Yusuf, and he sits down gratefully.

After lunch, Omar kindly offers to give Yusuf a quick tour of the school. He points out the library, the busy playground, and the classrooms.

By the end of that long day, Yusuf feels much less nervous than before. He has made one kind new friend. The new school already feels a little more like home.

versions.title: The New Student's First Day
versions.text:
Yusuf and his family recently moved from their old town to a busy new city, and today marks his first day at an unfamiliar school, a prospect that had been weighing on his mind for days beforehand. His stomach feels tight with apprehension, since he does not recognize a single person anywhere in the building, and he keeps wondering whether anyone will bother to acknowledge him at all.

Yusuf walks slowly into his new classroom, trying hard not to betray how nervous he feels inside. The other students already seem to have friends and familiar groups to sit beside, laughing about inside jokes that Yusuf cannot grasp yet, having arrived only this morning with no shared history to draw on. He slips quietly into a seat in the back row, feeling thoroughly isolated in the crowded, noisy room.

At lunchtime, Yusuf has no idea where he should sit. Every table in the busy cafeteria appears full of students talking, laughing, and exchanging jokes, and none of the groups seem to notice the new boy standing nearby. He stands there awkwardly holding his tray, growing more anxious with every passing second, wishing he could simply vanish into the crowd.

A classmate named Omar happens to glance over and notice Yusuf standing alone with nowhere obvious to go. Without hesitating, considerate toward new students by instinct, Omar waves him over and quickly makes room at his crowded table. "Come sit with us," he says, smiling in a genuinely warm way that instantly shifts Yusuf's perspective on the day. A sudden wave of relief washes over the reluctant newcomer, who sits down gratefully beside his new classmate.

After lunch, Omar kindly offers to give Yusuf a brief tour around the unfamiliar school, treating it almost as part of his normal daily routine rather than a special favor. He points out the quiet library, the busy playground, and the classrooms spread across each floor, explaining a little about each teacher along the way.

By the end of that long first day, Yusuf feels considerably less nervous than he did early that morning. He has already formed a genuine companionship with one classmate, and thanks to Omar's small, thoughtful act of kindness, this unfamiliar school is beginning to feel like a place where he truly belongs rather than a strange obligation he must simply endure.

versions.title: The New Student's First Day
versions.text:
Yusuf's first day at an unfamiliar school, following his family's recent relocation to a bustling new city, had been weighing heavily on his mind for days beforehand, a quiet dread that followed him through breakfast and the entire ride to school. His stomach tightens with apprehension the moment he steps inside, since he recognizes not a single person anywhere in the entire building, leaving him to wonder whether anyone will even bother to acknowledge his existence at all.

Entering his new classroom slowly, Yusuf tries hard not to betray how nervous he actually feels despite his considerable efforts to appear composed and unaffected. The other students already seem to possess established friendships and familiar groups, laughing about inside jokes Yusuf cannot possibly grasp, having arrived only that morning with no shared history to draw upon, no context for anything happening around him. He slips quietly into a seat in the back row, thoroughly isolated amid the crowded, unfamiliar faces surrounding him on every side.

Lunchtime brings its own distinct variety of anxiety, one that settles into his chest the moment he enters the cafeteria. Every table in the busy room appears occupied by students talking, laughing, and exchanging jokes, and none of the groups seem to register the new boy standing nearby at all, as though he were invisible. He stands there awkwardly holding his tray, growing increasingly anxious with each passing second, wishing he could simply vanish rather than be seen standing alone and conspicuously friendless.

A classmate named Omar happens to glance over and notice Yusuf's predicament immediately, something in his manner suggesting this is not the first time he has noticed someone struggling. Without hesitating, considerate toward new students by apparent instinct, Omar waves him over and promptly makes room at his own crowded table. "Come sit with us," he offers, smiling warmly in a manner that instantly shifts Yusuf's entire perspective on the day. Relief washes over the previously reluctant newcomer, who sits down gratefully, already feeling considerably less hesitant about what remains ahead.

Following lunch, Omar offers a brief tour of the unfamiliar building, treating the gesture almost as routine rather than as a special favor carrying any real obligation, as though welcoming newcomers were simply part of who he was. He points out the library, the outdoor playground, and the various classrooms distributed across each floor, explaining a little about each teacher and subject along the way, as though welcoming Yusuf into something larger than a single conversation.

By the day's conclusion, Yusuf feels considerably less nervous than he did that morning. He has formed a genuine companionship with one classmate, and thanks to Omar's small, thoughtful act of kindness, this unfamiliar school is gradually beginning to feel like a place where he truly belongs, rather than a strange obligation to be endured alone, day after day, until something eventually changed for the better.

keyWords.definition: friendly, caring, and helpful toward others

questions.stem: What is this story mostly about?

A boy who gets lost walking to his new school and calls his mom
A teacher who plans a surprise class party for the whole school

LOW.prompt: Has anyone ever helped you feel welcome when you were somewhere new? Explain what happened using at least two details from the story to support your ideas.
checklist: I clearly described my experience or idea.
I used at least two details from the story.
I wrote complete sentences with capital letters and periods.
LOW.modelAnswer: Yes, I remember a time when a classmate helped me feel welcome, just like Omar helped Yusuf in the story. In the story, Omar made room at his table so Yusuf did not have to sit alone, and then he showed Yusuf around the school. That small act of kindness helped Yusuf feel less nervous. I think even a small, friendly action can make a new student feel like they belong.

MID.prompt: Explain how Yusuf's feelings change from the beginning of the story to the end. Use at least two details from the story.

I used at least two details from the story.

MID.modelAnswer: At the beginning of the story, Yusuf feels nervous and anxious because he does not recognize anyone at his new, unfamiliar school, and he feels especially alone and worried while standing in the crowded cafeteria. His feelings change when Omar notices him and invites him to sit down, and Yusuf feels gratefully relieved. After Omar shows him around the school, Yusuf feels much less nervous and starts to feel like he could belong there, which shows how much one classmate's kindness can change someone's day.

keyWords.definition: the comfort or friendship that comes from spending time with someone
keyWords.example: The two neighbors found companionship in their daily walks together.

keyWords.definition: a duty or responsibility that someone feels they must fulfill
keyWords.example: She felt no real obligation to help, yet she offered anyway out of kindness.

keyWords.definition: a particular way of thinking about or viewing a situation
keyWords.example: Hearing her classmate's story completely changed his perspective on the problem.

keyWords.definition: unwilling or hesitant to do something
keyWords.example: He was reluctant to raise his hand, even though he knew the answer.

keyWords.definition: a natural tendency to act a certain way without having to think it through
keyWords.example: Helping a crying child seemed to come to her by instinct.

HIGH.prompt: The poll says a small act of kindness, like sharing a seat at lunch, can make a big difference to someone new. Do you agree or disagree? Support your argument with evidence from the story about Yusuf's isolation, Omar's instinct to help, and the shift in Yusuf's perspective.
checklist: I stated a clear position on the poll statement.
I supported my position with specific evidence from the story.
I addressed at least one point someone might make against my view.
HIGH.modelAnswer: I agree that a small act of kindness can make a big difference to someone new. In the story, Yusuf feels deeply isolated, unable to share in his classmates' inside jokes and growing anxious while standing alone in the cafeteria, until Omar, almost by instinct, invites him to sit down and later gives him a brief tour. This single gesture shifts Yusuf's entire perspective, turning his feeling of obligation to simply endure the day into a genuine sense of companionship and belonging. Someone might argue that a nervous student needs more than one kind classmate to truly feel at home, and that is probably true over time, but the story shows that such lasting comfort has to start somewhere, and a single reluctant newcomer's turning point can begin with just one small, unhesitating gesture.
